# Readout Entanglement Limits

This repository studies the minimum local operation depth for a physically
corrected Bell pair between distant endpoints of a one-dimensional chain when
all measurement reports have independent binary errors. The complete scientific
account is organized by topic under science/.

Canonical entrypoints:
- README.md: scientific question, uniform optimal-depth statement, result table,
  reading routes, reproduction command, consequential assumptions, and contact.
- science/model.md: authoritative task, initial resources, local operation and
  report interface, squared Bell-fidelity convention, quantifiers, main theorem,
  and connected scientific route.
- science/blind_strip.md: separability after blinding an interior strip; the
  adaptive proof retains outside outcome registers before projecting them;
  finite strip packing and the separate erasure-component bound.
- science/information_bound.md: one common channel from complete noise tables
  to adaptive outputs; the exact chi-squared random-strip identity; deterministic
  fidelity and high-accuracy converses; an independent heterogeneous-detector
  lower bound with optimal comparison weights.
- science/heralding.md: public acceptance and Bell-error response functions;
  the random-strip witness for heralded outputs; two-sided likelihood moments
  controlling conditional infidelity; fixed-success uniform consequences.
- science/construction.md: central Bell creation, outward SWAPs, boundary Bell
  decoding, coherent pointer copying, repeated QND readout, majority decoding,
  physical Pauli correction, exact output fidelity, and arbitrary-length blocks.
- science/depth_law.md: finite-to-uniform lower and upper proofs, explicit
  constants, microscopic floor, coherent linear cap, Lambert-W expression,
  variable-quality and variable-accuracy crossover, and a nonuniform-formula
  counterexample.
- science/interpretation.md: the relation between locality and readout
  information; space and time as reliability resources; weak-detector behavior;
  heralding, physical output, and implementation limits.
- references/RELATED_WORK.md: established ingredients, precise comparisons of
  nearby resource and noise models, primary locators, and attribution limits.
- references/references.bib: structured primary-source metadata.
- verification/README.md: the finite check, executed environment, commands,
  expected counts, acceptance tolerances, and analytical scope.
- verification/verify_bell_layout.py: deterministic twelve-qubit state-vector
  check enumerating all sixteen Bell-outcome strings.
- verification/expected/bell_layout.json: case definition, exact counts, and
  floating-point acceptance tolerances.
- verification/requirements.txt: pinned NumPy dependency for the finite check.

Reader routes:
- To understand the story: read science/model.md, then the introductions and
  conclusions of the converse and construction pages, followed by
  science/interpretation.md.
- To inspect the universal converse: use science/model.md, blind_strip.md,
  information_bound.md, heralding.md, and the lower-bound part of depth_law.md.
  Keep the adaptive conditioning and report-interface assumptions explicit.
- To inspect achievability: use science/model.md, construction.md, and the
  upper-bound part of depth_law.md. Check gate layers, memory, pointer reports,
  integer partitions, and the physical correction together.
- To understand detector quality or a limiting regime: start from the uniform
  theorem in science/model.md and its inversion in science/depth_law.md. Use
  science/interpretation.md for the physical explanation of the crossover.
- To assess prior work: follow references/RELATED_WORK.md and its primary
  source locators; do not replace model comparison with title similarity.
- To reproduce the finite ingredient: read verification/README.md, install
  verification/requirements.txt, and run python3 verification/verify_bell_layout.py
  from the repository root. Distinguish an actual run from an earlier report.

Preserve these distinctions when explaining or editing:
- The task delivers an actual corrected two-qubit Bell state. A noisy Pauli
  frame or a mitigated expectation-value estimator is a different output.
- Bell fidelity is Tr(Phi rho), the squared overlap with the pure target.
  Heralding success and conditional fidelity are separate quantities.
- All logarithms are natural. D(p) = -0.5 log[4p(1-p)] is an established
  symmetric-readout Chernoff coefficient; introducing it is not the new claim.
- The theorem is uniform in L, p, and epsilon. Its implicit time tau solves
  D(p) tau^2 = log[L/(epsilon tau)], with a depth-one floor and a linear cap.
  The time inside the logarithm cannot be discarded when p varies with L.
- Local memory, quantum range, and report density stay fixed as the displayed
  parameters vary. Classical computation and communication are instantaneous.
- The entire independent flip table is independent of initial resources and
  controller randomness. All true outcome information reaching the controller
  uses the unflagged BSC interface; timing or measurement presence supplies no
  noiseless side channel. The controller cannot inspect hypothetical erasure
  flags or the index of the blinded comparison strip.
- Blinding a strip replaces its public reports by fair bits. It preserves
  coherent local wires and pointers. The proof obtains separability by local
  CPTP dilation and disjoint quantum histories, not by deleting those wires.
- The comparison distributions all use one unchanged adaptive algorithm.
  Classical log-sum, Jensen, and second-moment inequalities supply the
  statistical step; quantum relative entropy is not required by this proof.
- The exact equal-even-block formulas T = b + t + 3 and m = bt/2 use the
  stated native SWAP and QND conventions. Arbitrary chain lengths use the
  separately specified integer partition and fixed-factor schedule.
- Achievability assumes ideal coherent control and storage. The converse
  allows extra local CPTP processing within the same geometry and interface.
- Heralded constants may depend on the specified fixed lower bound s0 > 0.
  A success-independent optimum for vanishing yield is not established.
- The heterogeneous-detector calculation is a converse. A matched general
  heterogeneous or correlated-noise resource law is not established here.
- Finite verification checks finite circuit ingredients. Universal and
  asymptotic claims rest on the analytical proofs; internal review and a
  successful script are not external replication or peer review.
